candidate.source_a: Calcium phosphate forms crystalline deposits in bone tissue through osteoblast-mediated mineralization.
candidate.source_b: Marine diatoms precipitate silica-based cell walls using enzymatic silicatein proteins.

counterfactuals: If Source A didn't mention osteoblast-mediated mineralization, the connection between biological processes and inorganic formation would be weaker.
If Source B didn't mention enzymatic silicatein proteins, the enzyme-templated aspect would be missing.
Without both sources, we wouldn't have examples of biological systems creating inorganic structures through enzymatic processes.

evidence_assessment.notes: GLiREL correctly identified key relations in both sources. Source A shows osteoblast-mediated mineralization of calcium phosphate (enzyme-templated inorganic formation). Source B shows enzymatic silicatein proteins precipitating silica structures (enzyme-templated inorganic formation). Each source independently supports the candidate concept.
